metrics.n: DAX measures live in the semantic model as TMDL or TOM objects. The ontology item imports them as metrics (Preview).

dimensions.n: Columns, hierarchies, display folders, sort-by-column and perspectives are declared in TMDL.

relationships.n: Declared model relationships (fromColumn, toColumn). Copilot still uses them for fields outside the AI data schema.

synonyms.n: AI instructions, synonyms, descriptions read by Copilot and data agent. Prep data for AI is Preview.

verifiedQueries.n: Verified answers bind phrases to visuals (Preview). Data agent takes question-query pairs for SQL and KQL sources, not semantic models.

nl2sql.n: Copilot in Power BI is GA. Data agent does NL2SQL, NL2DAX, NL2KQL; docs conflict on GA or Preview.

ontology.n: Ontology item: entity types, relationships, rules, metrics, data bindings. Preview since Ignite, November 2025.

graph.n: GQL over OneLake; GA per a Fabric blog post I could not fetch. Data agent NL2GQL source is Preview.

vector.n: SQL database in Fabric: GA vector type and vector index. Data agent reads Azure AI Search index (Preview).

mcp.n: Fabric IQ MCP is GA and read-only. Authoring MCP: local GA, hosted Preview. Ontology MCP is Preview.

governance.n: RLS and OLS apply via Fabric IQ MCP; RLS and CLS via data agent. Verified answers are no security boundary.

openStandard.n: TMDL is a documented text format. Ossie converter is initial and open source. Ontology imports RDF, OWL (Preview).

offers: Power BI semantic models hold DAX measures, relationships, hierarchies, descriptions and synonyms in TMDL text files under Git.
Prep data for AI saves AI instructions, AI data schema and verified answers in the model for Copilot and agents.
Fabric data agent turns questions into SQL, DAX or KQL over up to five sources, with instructions and example queries.
Fabric IQ MCP (GA) is a read-only remote server: schema lookup, value search and DAX execution under the caller's RLS.
Ontology (Preview) models entities, relationships, rules and DAX-backed metrics, and binds them to lakehouse, warehouse and SQL sources.
Graph in Fabric runs GQL over OneLake tables; the data agent can use it as a source (Preview).
gaps: Prep data for AI and the ontology item are Preview; Learn pages disagree on some GA labels.
Data agent accepts no example queries for semantic models; verified answers are visual-based, capped at 250 per model.
Q&A retires (February 2027 on most Learn pages, December 2026 on one); Prep data for AI still requires Q&A enabled.
Data agent replies cap at 25 rows and 25 columns, English only, read-only, up to five sources.
Fabric IQ MCP covers reports and semantic models only; it does not support ontologies or data agents.
fillWith: Semantic Link Labs (Best Practice Analyzer, TMDL edits from notebooks)
Fabric data agent Python SDK (evaluation against question-answer pairs)
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Publish a Fabric data agent over a Power BI semantic model, and keep AI instructions, AI data schema and verified answers in Prep data for AI, because the DAX tool ignores data agent level instructions for semantic models. For lakehouse or warehouse tables, add data source instructions and example queries to the data agent. Test the generated DAX or SQL with the data agent Python SDK, then expose the agent through its MCP endpoint or use Fabric IQ MCP for read-only DAX access.

snippet.title: TMDL table with a description, a DAX measure and a relationship
snippet.code:
/// Sales fact table
table Sales

    /// Sum of quantity times net price
    measure 'Sales Amount' = SUMX('Sales', 'Sales'[Quantity] * 'Sales'[Net Price])
        formatString: $ #,##0

    column 'Product Key'
        dataType: int64
        isHidden
        sourceColumn: ProductKey

relationship cdb6e6a9-c9d1-42b9-b9e0-484a1bc7e123
    fromColumn: Sales.'Product Key'
    toColumn: Product.'Product Key'

metrics.n: No metric or measure object in the T-SQL docs reviewed. Use views or an external semantic layer.

dimensions.n: No declared dimensions, hierarchies or time grains. Star schema exists only as table design.

relationships.n: Foreign keys and SQL graph edge tables declare joins. Fabric SQL database Copilot reads PK and FK metadata.

synonyms.n: AGENTS.md extended properties hold business rules per object. I found only GitHub Copilot in SSMS reading them.

verifiedQueries.n: No verified question-to-SQL store. SQL MCP Server uses configured entities, not example queries.

nl2sql.n: GitHub Copilot in SSMS is GA (March 2026). It is an IDE tool, not an in-database or embeddable API.

ontology.n: No ontology or class model in the engine. SQL graph tables store nodes and edges as data, not business classes.

graph.n: SQL Graph node and edge tables with ASCII-art MATCH syntax. SHORTEST_PATH needs SQL Server 2019 or later.

vector.n: Vector type and VECTOR_DISTANCE: GA. Vector index and VECTOR_SEARCH: GA in Azure SQL Database, Preview in SQL Server 2025.

mcp.n: SQL MCP Server is part of Data API builder, an open source separate product you host. No NL2SQL by design.

governance.n: GitHub Copilot in SSMS runs queries under the user's login permissions. SQL MCP Server applies role-based entity permissions.

openStandard.n: No semantic-layer object to export or import. SQL Graph queries use the T-SQL MATCH syntax.

offers: Native vector type (float32 up to 1,998 dimensions, float16 up to 3,996) with VECTOR_DISTANCE for exact search.
AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS calls Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Ollama or ONNX models registered with CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL; AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS splits text.
SQL Graph node and edge tables with MATCH and SHORTEST_PATH query connected data in T-SQL.
GitHub Copilot in SSMS (GA) writes T-SQL from natural language and reads database instructions stored as AGENTS.md extended properties.
SQL MCP Server (Data API builder) exposes configured entities with descriptions, roles and seven DML tools; no NL2SQL by design.
gaps: No semantic model, metric, dimension or ontology object found in the SQL Server 2025 or Azure SQL docs.
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL accepts only MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS. No NL-to-SQL function appears in the T-SQL docs reviewed.
Copilot in Azure SQL Database status is unclear: one page says preview for early adopters, a blog title says GA.
Vector index and VECTOR_SEARCH are Preview on SQL Server 2025 and need PREVIEW_FEATURES; GA in Azure SQL Database.
SQL Graph does not support cross-database queries, temporal tables or memory-optimized tables.
fillWith: Power BI semantic model via Fabric mirroring
vendors.nl2sqlPath: The engine has no built-in NL-to-SQL for applications, so teams either call an LLM from the app with schema and business rules in the prompt, or expose configured entities through SQL MCP Server, which skips NL2SQL on purpose. For interactive work, use GitHub Copilot in SSMS and store business rules as AGENTS.md extended properties. For governed metrics, mirror the data into Fabric and use a Power BI semantic model with a data agent.

notes.topic: Fabric IQ and ontology: existence, announcement, status
notes.text: Fabric IQ and its Ontology item were announced at Ignite in November 2025, with ontology in public preview. Microsoft Learn (pages updated 2026-07 to 2026-10) still labels the IQ workload and ontology Preview, and says the old ontology experience retires on 2027-01-31. Microsoft Fabric blog posts from Build (June 2026) describe Fabric IQ, Graph and Operations agents as GA with ontology still in Preview; I could not fetch those posts (HTTP 403) and relied on search snippets.

notes.topic: Ontology details that matter for NL-to-SQL builders
notes.text: Ontology stores definitions and bindings; it is not a query engine, and the bound source (semantic model, lakehouse, eventhouse, warehouse, SQL database, mirrored database) runs the query. DAX measures from a semantic model appear as metrics, rules are natural-language text, and graph execution is an opt-in materialization. A data agent can mount an ontology (Preview) and then writes source-native SQL, KQL or DAX.

notes.text: Fabric IQ names the workload (ontology, semantic model, graph, data agent, operations agent, plan), a remote MCP server for Power BI reports and semantic models, and a Copilot mode in the Power BI report viewer. Fabric IQ MCP does not support ontologies or data agents; a separate Ontology MCP server (Preview) and a data-agent MCP endpoint exist. In the report viewer, Copilot does not return verified answers when Fabric IQ is on.

notes.topic: Power BI MCP servers: renames and replacements
notes.text: Current docs describe one Power BI Authoring MCP server with hosted (Preview) and local (GA) options; earlier coverage called the local server the Power BI Modeling MCP server, and the npm package is still named powerbi-modeling-mcp. The earlier hosted query endpoint (api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/powerbi) is now called the Power BI Consumption MCP server and is kept only for existing integrations; Microsoft points consumption to Fabric IQ MCP (https://fabriciq.svc.cloud.microsoft/v1/mcp/fabriciq). Fabric also lists remote MCP servers for Core, Data Warehouse (T-SQL), Eventhouse (KQL), Activator and operations agent, plus local servers for development and Real-Time Intelligence; I did not check the status label of each.

notes.topic: Power BI Q&A retirement and linguistic schema
notes.text: Learn pages say Q&A experiences go away in February 2027, but the data agent semantic model guide says Q&A retires in December 2026. notes.topic: Fabric data agent: status conflict and what it reads
notes.text: The data agent concept page (updated 2026-10-21) calls it generally available, but the Release status table (updated 2026-07) lists Data agent under Data Science as Preview; a secondary source puts GA at FabCon in March 2026, which I did not confirm. Sources can be up to five lakehouses, warehouses, KQL databases, semantic models, mirrored databases, ontologies or (Preview) graph and Azure AI Search. For semantic models, the DAX tool uses only model metadata and Prep data for AI settings and ignores data agent level instructions; Topics and schema object descriptions for SQL sources are Preview on the preview runtime.

notes.text: Unified Catalog glossary terms sit under governance domains, can carry synonyms, acronyms and related terms, and can carry policies that follow the term to data products and assets. Linking terms to assets and columns is labeled preview, and asset curation requires migrating classic terms first. I found no Microsoft doc where Copilot in Power BI, the data agent or the ontology reads Unified Catalog terms, so treat the glossary as governance metadata, not AI context.

notes.topic: Open Semantic Interchange renamed Apache Ossie
notes.text: Search results show the Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) effort now appears as Apache Ossie (incubating). A Snowflake engineering blog dated 2026-09-30 describes an initial open source converter between Power BI/Fabric semantic models and Ossie, with DAX added as a recognized expression language; the post does not state a preview or GA status. A Fabric community post titled 'Microsoft + Snowflake's commitment to Apache Ossie' exists, but I did not open it.

notes.topic: SQL Server 2025: no native semantic layer object
notes.text: SQL Server 2025 went generally available on 2025-11-18 with the vector type, text chunking, embeddings through CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL, and DiskANN indexing. I found no semantic model, metric, dimension or ontology object in the SQL Server 2025 or Azure SQL docs; this is an absence in what I reviewed, not a proof. The closest native items are the AGENTS.md and CONSTITUTION.md extended properties, which only GitHub Copilot in SSMS is documented to read.

notes.text: SQL MCP Server is part of open source Data API builder (version 1.7 and later; 2.0 is current), is self-hosted, and states that it intentionally does not support NL2SQL. It exposes seven DML tools over configured entities, so entity description text is the only semantic context an agent gets, and it covers data operations rather than schema changes. The docs carry no preview or GA label.
